summary: Marks content as generated by AI, and opens what that means — what was generated, from what, and what to check. The explanation is required.
useWhen: content a model wrote is shown as part of the product — a summary, a drafted reply, a suggested field value, a generated description
a person has edited generated content, and it should still say where it came from

useInstead.when: the content is an answer to a question someone asked, with sources
useInstead.why: in the AssistantAnswer pattern the answer already says it is generated — its Citations and ConfidenceIndicator carry what to trust; add an AILabel only where the answer leaves the conversation and is shown elsewhere

useInstead.when: the reader needs to know how far to trust it
useInstead.why: AILabel says who made it, not how good it is; pair them when both matter, and never let the mark stand in for a trust level

useInstead.when: an agent is doing something now
useInstead.why: that is a run in progress; AILabel marks finished content

useInstead.when: the explanation has nothing to do with AI
useInstead.why: AILabel is a Toggletip whose button is the AI mark; for any other explanation use the ⓘ

composition.note: Place it right after the heading or label of the generated content, not inside the content. Name it for the content — `aria-label="About this summary"` — and the button reads "AI: About this summary". The children say what was generated, from what — the model, the inputs — and what to check before relying on it; at most one Link, to how it is made. Set `isEdited` once a person has changed the content; clear it only if the content is generated again.
composition.example: Summary Written by atlas-m from the last 20 runs. Check the failure counts against the Runs tab before sharing. How summaries are made

sm.use: beside body-sm text — table cells, field labels, card titles; drawn 20px, a 24px target

md.use: beside body text and headings — the default

top.use: the default — above the mark, clear of the content below

bottom.use: near the top of the viewport; it also flips here on its own

left.use: beside a label at the end of a row

right.use: beside a label at the start of a row

children.note: the explanation, under a heading — "Generated by AI", or "Generated by AI, edited by a person" when edited; read out on open

labels.note: mark, edited, title and editedTitle, for translation; the button's name follows the translated mark

a11y.role: button (a disclosure) that opens a status region
guarantees: the button's name starts with the visible mark — "AI: About this summary", or "AI, Edited: …" — so what is seen is what is heard (WCAG 2.5.3)
the explanation behaves as Toggletip's: opened by a press, not hover; read out on open while focus stays on the mark; Tab reaches a link inside; Escape closes it and returns focus
it is not modal: it never traps focus or hides the page
the mark uses the primary colour role, not a status colour: it says who made the content, not that something is wrong or new
requires: `aria-label` naming the content it marks — "About this summary", not "AI info"
children that say what was generated and from what
notes: It labels; it does not detect. Whether content is generated, and whether a person has edited it since, is the caller's knowledge — pass it, never guess it.

antiPatterns.dont: an explanation that says only "This was generated by AI"
antiPatterns.do: the model, what it read, and what to check
antiPatterns.why: the mark already says that; an explanation with nothing behind it is a claim the system cannot back

antiPatterns.dont: leaving the mark unchanged after a person edits the content
antiPatterns.why: the reader is told the model wrote words a person chose, and blames or trusts the wrong author

antiPatterns.dont: one AILabel for a whole page of mixed content
antiPatterns.why: the reader cannot tell which parts were generated; mark each generated piece where it starts

antiPatterns.dont: a mark on every row of a list that is all generated
antiPatterns.do: one AILabel on the list's heading
antiPatterns.why: twenty identical marks are noise, and twenty tab stops in the way of the rows

antiPatterns.dont: using the mark as a badge for an AI feature — a button, a menu item, a nav link
antiPatterns.why: it marks content a model produced; on a feature it says nothing about any content, and teaches readers to ignore it
